comments.note: WindowsFileLauncherService.ShowInExplorer (Services/WindowsFileLauncherService.cs) constructs the explorer /select argument by interpolating the file path directly: /select,"filePath". If a future file path contains embedded double-quotes (unusual but technically valid on Windows via paths like NTFS alternate data streams), the argument could be malformed. Recommend documenting the path-no-quotes assumption or sanitising via Path.GetFullPath before argument construction.

AvaloniaMoviePropertiesService (Services/AvaloniaMoviePropertiesService.cs) ignores the CancellationToken parameter passed to ShowAsync — consistent with how AvaloniaFilterManagerService handles it, since ShowDialog has no built-in cancellation support. Consider documenting this limitation in the XML doc as a known constraint, or registering a token callback to close the dialog programmatically.

MoviePropertiesViewModel.FileCreated (ViewModels/MoviePropertiesViewModel.cs) formats the DateTime as yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss using a hard-coded format string. All other date formatting across the codebase currently happens in AXAML via StringFormat bindings. For consistency, a future improvement could move formatting to the view layer; for now the invariant format avoids culture-dependent display issues.

summary: Reviewed 7 source files across Services, ViewModels, and Views layers. 0 Critical, 0 High, 0 Medium, 1 Low (argument injection risk in ShowInExplorer — Low severity, no code execution path). Security sign-off: PASS.

comments.note: Low | A03 Injection | src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/WindowsFileLauncherService.cs line 22 | ShowInExplorer constructs the explorer.exe Arguments string via direct interpolation: $"/select,\"{filePath}\"". A path containing embedded double-quote characters (theoretically valid on NTFS) would produce a malformed argument. Since UseShellExecute=true targets explorer.exe directly (no shell interpreter involved), there is no code execution path — worst outcome is explorer navigating to the wrong location or failing silently. Exploitability requires an attacker to have already written a malicious path to the database (far higher-severity breach). Remediation: call Path.GetFullPath(filePath) to normalise the path before interpolation, or use ProcessStartInfo.ArgumentList (collection-based argument construction) which handles quoting automatically.

Info | A03 Injection | src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/WindowsFileLauncherService.cs line 14 | OpenFolder passes the DataFolder path as the sole Arguments value without quoting. DataFolder is sourced from IAppPaths.MovieDataDirectory(movie.Hash) where Hash is an application-computed hex string (no metacharacters). In practice this is safe; however, wrapping the argument in double-quotes ("\"{path}\"") would make the call robust against any future IAppPaths implementation that returns paths with spaces.

Info | A09 Logging | src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/WindowsFileLauncherService.cs | File-shell operations (OpenFolder, ShowInExplorer) produce no log output on failure. Process.Start returns null when the process cannot be launched; the result is currently discarded (_ = Process.Start(...)). Logging a warning on null return would improve diagnostic visibility without security impact.

comments.note: Fix-Forward applied to src/VideoIndexer.App/Program.cs (section 5.75 UI dialog services): the identical Func<Window?> ownerFactory lambda was defined three separate times inside individual AddSingleton factory lambdas (for AvaloniaConnectionEditorService, AvaloniaFilterManagerService, and AvaloniaMoviePropertiesService). Hoisted to a single shared local variable declared once before all three AddSingleton calls. Non-behavioral — all three singletons still lazily receive the same delegate. Eliminates future copy-paste risk when a fourth dialog service is registered.

[documentation-forward] AvaloniaMoviePropertiesService.ShowAsync (src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/AvaloniaMoviePropertiesService.cs): the cancellationToken parameter is silently ignored because Avalonia's ShowDialog has no built-in cancellation support. The XML doc on the parameter currently reads only 'Cancellation token.' — this should explicitly state that the token is not observed and that the dialog can only be dismissed by the user or programmatically via CloseRequested. Mirrors the same gap in AvaloniaFilterManagerService; both should be documented consistently.

WindowsFileLauncherService.OpenFolder (src/VideoIndexer.App/Services/WindowsFileLauncherService.cs line 14): the Arguments value is the raw path string without quoting. In practice DataFolder is derived from IAppPaths.MovieDataDirectory(hash) where hash is a hex string with no spaces, so this is currently safe. Defence-in-depth: wrapping in double-quotes (e.g. Arguments = $"\"{path}\"") would guard against any future IAppPaths implementation returning a path with spaces. Security Auditor also noted this at Info level.

No observations on MoviePropertiesViewModel, MoviePropertiesView, IFileLauncherService, IMoviePropertiesService, or the test suite — all are clean, idiomatic, and consistent with codebase conventions.
